# Dhammadevaputtajātaka (Ja 457)

**ID:** Ja 457
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Dhammadevaputtajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul10.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhammadevaputtajātaka* (Ja 457), also referred to as the *Dhamma Jātaka*, is a canonical birth story set at Jetavana [Boriharnwanaket]. The narrative occasion arises when monks discuss Devadatta being swallowed by the earth on account of his enmity with the Tathāgata. The Buddha relates that in a previous existence Devadatta had likewise struck against the authority of righteousness, leading to him being swallowed into the nethermost hell. In that past life, the Bodhisatta appeared as the deity Dhamma (Dhammadevaputta) and contended with Adhamma (Devadatta's former birth) [Levman 2014; Boriharnwanaket]. The text features a verse debate between Right and Wrong, and contains the phrase *vāmam karoti* describing Adhamma making an adverse "leftwards circuit" around Jambudvīpa [Levman 2014; Boriharnwanaket]. In exegetical tradition, the Bodhisatta's birth as Dhammadevaputta is cited in the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā* as an illustration of the perfection of patience (*adhivāsanakkhanti*) [Endo 1997].

The text is referenced elsewhere in later Pali literature in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.4.7).

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Mentioned in: Mil 5.4.7 Kusalākusalasamavisamapañha

**Sources**

- [Endo 1997] Toshiichi Endo, Buddha in Theravada Buddhism. A Study of the Concept of Buddha in the Pali Commentaries (1997) — Attested the Bodhisatta's birth as Dhammadevaputta as an exemplar of the perfection of endurance-patience in the Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā.
- [Levman 2014] Bryan Geoffrey Levman, Linguistic Ambiguities, the Transmissional Process, and the Earliest Recoverable Language of Buddhism (2014) — Discussed the phrase vāmam karoti in Ja 457 regarding Adhamma's leftward circuit around Jambudvīpa.
- [Boriharnwanaket] Sujin Boriharnwanaket, Perfections Leading to Enlightenment — Cited Ja 457 under the alternative title Dhamma Jataka and noted stanzas shared with the Cariyāpiṭaka commentary.
